content.confidence: 3: You are fairly confident in your assessment. It is possible that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.
content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper, the authors propose a neighborhood point transformer (NPFormer) to perform point cloud geometry compression. NPFormer combines sparse convolution and point cloud transformer, and outputs a multi-stage occupancy probability prediction. Evaluated on both 3D object and LiDAR scan workloads, the proposed method shows higher compression ratio with much faster runtime compared with state-of-the-art PCG compression algorithms.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
- Good experiment results: better compression ratio with orders of magnitude faster decoding speed. 
- Evaluation is extensive: the authors cover both object and LiDAR point clouds.
- The NPFormer is easy to understand and clearly written.

Weaknesses:
- Technically I don't think NPFormer is quite novel. It seems like a simple combination of MinkowsiNet / sparseconvnet and point cloud transformers. I believe that the entire Section 3.2 has been studied in various previous papers (e.g. PointFormer, point cloud transformer, etc.) in different tasks. 
- It is not very clear what will happen if we remove one of the component (e.g. sparse convolution or attention) in NPFormer. 
- The details of the paper might be a bit hard to grasp for people not familiar in PCG compression. For example, how did you actually achieve compression? Is it the case that you store a point cloud with a coarser granularity and try to reconstruct the original point cloud with your NPFormer? If that is the case (which is my guess), then how do you differentiate your work with those papers in the field of 3D reconstruction, which also follow a similar intuition of predicting the occupancy probabilities?
- You mentioned that the decoding complexity of NPFormer is around 6 seconds. Is it for the entire sequence or a single scene on SemanticKITTI? If it is a single scene, it seems that NPFormer is still not usable in practice.

Question:
- Is your method applicable to indoor point cloud geometry compression? Also, do you only preserve geometric information or it is also possible for your method to take features (e.g. RGB / intensity) into consideration?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
- The writing about NPFormer is clear, but it will be better if the authors can provide more context about the task of PCG compression and the difference between PCG compression and point cloud reconstruction.
- The quality of experiments look good to me. I'm not an expert in PCG compression so I cannot judge the significance of the results.
- The novelty of NPFormer is fair, in terms of both the network architecture and the formulation of MOPA (Section 3.1).
- It seems that the authors did not provide source code along with the paper, so I cannot comment on the reproducibility.
content.summary_of_the_review: I think the paper deals with an important problem of point cloud geometry compression. The results look strong to me (6-bit ish per point for a LiDAR scan on SemanticKITTI, and better performance than SOTA). The major drawback of this paper is that NPFormer clearly lacks technical novelty and it seems that the speed is still a bit too slow (if 6 second is for one scene). The paper will also benefit from another round of refinement which adds in more details about the PCG compression task itself.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a deep learning-based 3D point cloud geometry compression framework built upon multi-scale sparse tensor representation structure. The major technical contribution lies in the proposed transformer-style local feature aggregation network (i.e., NPFormer), whose core is the neighborhood point attention (i.e., NPA) mechanism. Experiments show the superiority of the proposed compression framework over standardized G-PCC and other recent learning-based approaches. Besides, the overall processing pipeline achieves satisfactory running speed. In general, I am okay with the technical correctness as well as the experimental results. My major concern is the limited novelty of the proposed NPFormer, which is claimed by the authors as the core contribution of this work.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
One obvious strength of this paper is the good performance compared with previous methods. It also maintains satisfactory efficiency. However, the actual technical novelty is limited. 

Architecturally, the overall learning workflow inherits the previous work (i.e., SparsePCGC), and the major difference is the new transformer-style local feature aggregation module. Within the proposed NPFormer, there is also nothing new. The proposed neighborhood attention mechanism is just common practice in the point cloud transformer community. Applying transformer to a new task indeed has its value, but not that much.

Other issues are listed as follows:
1. More discussions about point cloud transformers should be provided.
2. Please explain more detailedly (in Eq.(4)) how Q and K_{kNN}^T are multiplied (the dimension of Q is N x d_e while the dimension of K_{KNN} is N x k x d_e). Is there any broadcasting operation?
3. In ablation studies, the authors should also verify the effectiveness of the proposed NPA module (or the whole NPFormer module) by replacing it with other basic version of local feature aggregation operation (e.g., point-wise MLP + max-pooling). The current ablative experiments are not very informative and important.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Although this paper formulates a clear presentation of the specific modules like NPFormer and NPA, it does not provide a detailed and clear description of the overall processing pipeline. The readers must refer to the previous work (SparsePCGC) for more details. This causes difficulties in understanding this paper. My biggest concern is the limited technical novelty.
content.summary_of_the_review: Although the proposed method achieves good performance, the novelty is quite limited.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper:
The author introduces several designs for point cloud compress as follows:

1. NPFormer block design combining sparse convolution and self-attention layer.
2. Neighborhood Point Attention layer, which takes neighbor points as a query set instead of a global or window partition.
3. Multi-scale and multi-stage point cloud probability approximation for point cloud decompress.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
**Strength**

The paper is well-written and organized.

**Weaknesses**

**1. Novelty**

**a)** The author claims the NPFormer block combines sparse convolution and self-attention layers. But actually, they just simply replace the first linear-norm-act lay in the Point Transformer block with two sparse convolution layers. Meanwhile, there is no difficulty or breakthrough in technique implementation.

**b)** The author claims that they proposed a neighborhood point attention (NPA) layer, which takes neighbor points as a query set, but the original design in Point Transformer is neighborhood attention. The only difference is that NPA applies normal multi-head dot-product attention instead of vector attention proposed in SAN.

**c)** The author claims they propose multi-scale (mainly) and multi-stage point cloud probability approximation, while multi-scale probability approximation has already been proposed by [MSVoxelDNN](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2104.09859.pdf) MSVoxelDNN was adopted as a comparison of previous state-of-art work ([OctAttention](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/19942)).

**2. Experiments**

**a)** The ablation study only contains attention head study and neighborhood number study. There is no ablation for multi-scale and multi-stage probability approximation. The number of stage ablation and visualization of each stage (scale) are also significant. The influence of replacing the first linear-norm-act lay in the Point Transformer block with a convolution layer is also not available.

**b)** There is no comparison with previous state-of-art work (OctAttention) in LiDAR PCGs. The author only compares object PCGs results.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper writing is clear, but the novelty is the main drawback, as mentioned in Weaknesses.
content.summary_of_the_review: The majority of contributions claimed by the paper are not novel, and the paper also lacks detailed experiments.

content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
